acts.name: Monologue
acts.function: hook and setup: a retired star, deadpan, to camera, talks about a bitter taste that only the real ones appreciate; the slow pull-back reveals him piece by piece

acts.name: The win
acts.function: payoff: 'getting your lick back' made literal, a 3.25 s championship montage of 9 cuts (avg 0.36 s) slammed in on the music, with the one firework stadium shot at its peak

acts.name: The sip
acts.function: punchline: back in the quiet room, he sips, grins, 'Tastes good, don't it?'

acts.name: End card
acts.function: tagline then brand mark on a teal glitter cloud

shots.subject_in_frame: 0.0 s: extreme close-up of mouth and chin only, mouth centred at x 50%, y 45%, lower face fills 75% of the width, frame top cuts just below the sunglasses, saucer rim in the bottom 8%. 2.2 s: sunglasses enter: face 55% of width, eyes at y 22%. 4.85 s: close-up, face 38% of width, beanie top cropped. 7.2 s: face 30%. 10.74 s (board s01): medium close-up, face 25% of width centred at x 48%, sunglasses at y 33%, beanie top touches the top edge, shoulders fill the bottom 40%, brick wall behind. 12.9 s: face 19%, red cup enters bottom left held at chest. 15.3 s: face 15%, black picture frame enters top right. 21.35 s (board s01b): medium shot seated, body 38% of the width centred at x 44%, head top at y 10%, face 12% of the width, cup held at chest height x 40% y 70%, picture frame top right at x 82-93%, y 8-28%.
shots.camera: starts at mouth height and ends at chest height looking very slightly up (5 deg low angle), square to the wall; normal-to-long lens feel (~85 mm at the start, ~50 mm equivalent at the end), shallow depth of field: wall soft while close, nearly sharp at the end
shots.camera_move: one continuous slow pull-back with a slight rise, 0.0-21.48 s, framing width grows about 6x (scale 1.0 -> 0.17 of the subject), steady and linear with a slightly faster first 2 s (tilts up from mouth to eyes 0-2.2 s). No pan. It reveals in order: mouth (0 s), sunglasses (2 s), beanie (5 s), shoulders (8 s), the red cup (12.5 s), the picture on the wall (14.5 s), the whole seated figure (21 s).
shots.action: Sits facing camera, nearly still, delivering a deadpan monologue straight into the lens in a low, unhurried voice: 0.35 'I ain't even going to hold you.' 2.69 'Bitter really is an acquired taste.' 5.60 'That's how you know it's not for everybody.' 7.40 'But the real ones know what that flavor is.' 10.93 'When you get to the bottom of that mug,' 13.19 'when ain't nothing left but that grit,' 15.76 'that's where you really appreciate that grind.' 17.99 'Because nothing tastes as good as getting your lick back.' (ends 21.70, over shot 2). Small head tilts on the stressed words, a slight knowing smirk on 'real ones' and 'lick back'; from ~12 s he holds the red cup in his right hand at chest height without drinking.
shots.light: single soft warm key from camera left at 45 deg, warm tungsten ~3200 K, falling off hard to the right; brick wall raked warm, edges near black; measured brightness 31 at the start, 39 mid, 35 end (0-255); dominant colour #29201d
shots.out: hard cut on the music downbeat to shot 2 while the last word 'back' is still sounding (voice runs 0.22 s over the cut)
shots.audio: dry close-miked voice, deadpan, ~-22 LUFS mean, phrases separated by 0.4-1.0 s pauses of low room tone (~-45 dBFS); no music audible. Lines L01-L08 at their absolute times (set/lines.json).
shots.render: one locked setup rendered as 8 takes, one per line (cut30 shots 1-8): first frame + guide_audio from that line's clip (set/lines/L01.wav ... L08.wav, placed at the line's offset inside the take). Each take's first frame is a plate of char_vet in loc_brick_wall at that take's start framing (subject_in_frame gives the face width at each take start), and its prompt asks for the same slow pull-back continuing. Cut on the line breaks (the pauses). If a take drifts off the framing or the face changes, re-render it on the same first frame and guide audio; never use reference mode for this setup.

lines.kind: on-camera speech (sync, mouth in extreme close-up)

lines.words: Bitter really is an acquired taste.
That's how you know it's not for everybody.
But the real ones know what that flavor is.
When you get to the bottom of that mug,
when ain't nothing left but that grit,
that's where you really appreciate that grind.
Because nothing tastes as good as getting your lick back.
